40631332.clinical_problem: identifying clinically acquired brain MRIs with limited imaging pathology, to repurpose them as 'clinical controls' for pediatric neuroimaging AI research
40631332.patient_population: clinical brain MRI archive at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (over 250,000 scans)
40631332.model_description: A systematic, machine-assisted protocol has non-clinician graders review radiology reports and grade clinically acquired pediatric brain MRIs for presence/absence of significant pathology and image-quality concerns, to curate large-scale clinical-control datasets for AI and neuroimaging research.

40650736.clinical_problem: reducing pediatric brain MRI scan time and the need for sedation while maintaining diagnostic image quality
40650736.patient_population: 116 pediatric participants (mean age 7.9 years), single center
40650736.model_description: Deep learning reconstruction is applied to accelerate brain MRI acquisition; image quality, artifacts, noise and lesion conspicuity are compared by pediatric radiologists between conventional, conventional-plus-DLR, and accelerated-plus-DLR protocols.
40650736.headline_result: 43% scan-time reduction with accelerated DLR; 100% lesion detection rate across all three reconstructions

40653922.clinical_problem: screening for ileocolic intussusception on abdominal radiographs to triage which children need further ultrasound evaluation
40653922.patient_population: pediatric patients aged 5 years or younger across 4 hospitals
40653922.model_description: An AI model, retrained and upgraded with additional multicenter data, screens abdominal radiographs for ileocolic intussusception and is evaluated as a standalone tool and as assistance to radiologists of varying experience levels.
40653922.dataset_size: 746 plus 431 training patients; 68 and 90 external validation patients (hospitals C, D)
40653922.headline_result: External validation: sensitivity 81.7%, specificity 81.7%, AUC 86.2%; with AI assistance radiologist specificity improved from 77.1% to 93%
40653922.study_design: retrospective multicenter external validation with reader study

40670194.model_family: radiomics (Bagging Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, Stochastic Gradient Descent)
40670194.clinical_problem: identifying high-risk hepatoblastoma per the CHIC risk-stratification system from contrast-enhanced CT to guide treatment
40670194.patient_population: 162 children with pathologically diagnosed hepatoblastoma, single center
40670194.model_description: A CT radiomics model, built from features extracted from pre-treatment venous-phase contrast-enhanced CT and evaluated with three machine learning classifiers, predicts high-risk hepatoblastoma status per the CHIC-HS risk stratification system.

40670764.clinical_problem: improving intracardiac visualization on pediatric cardiac CT angiography for congenital heart disease under free-breathing conditions
40670764.patient_population: 91 pediatric patients aged 1-10 years suspected of congenital heart disease, single center
40670764.model_description: Super-resolution deep learning reconstruction is compared against conventional deep learning reconstruction and hybrid iterative reconstruction for pediatric cardiac CT angiography acquired under free breathing, assessed for image quality and diagnostic accuracy of congenital heart disease.
40670764.headline_result: SR-DLR accuracy 99.12%, sensitivity 99.07%, exceeding conventional DLR and hybrid iterative reconstruction

40676171.clinical_problem: distinguishing individuals with ADHD from healthy controls and identifying affected brain networks using structural connectivity
40676171.patient_population: 947 individuals aged 7-26 years across 8 centers, ADHD-200 dataset
40676171.model_description: A transformer-based deep learning model constructs structural brain connectivity networks from MRI, using standardized regional data sequences, to distinguish individuals with ADHD from healthy controls and identify altered connectivity regions.

40685764.clinical_problem: providing reliable, fast automated brain volumetric segmentation and age-specific reference growth charts for healthy children
40685764.model_description: FastSurfer, a deep-learning-based brain segmentation tool, is validated against FreeSurfer in a multicenter pediatric cohort and used to generate age-specific reference growth charts for 15 anatomical brain regions.
40685764.release_evidence: The morphometric data, growth charts, and code are publicly accessible
40685764.headline_result: Mean Dice similarity coefficient 0.90, relative volume difference 0.3%, ICC 0.87 versus FreeSurfer

40718817.clinical_problem: using machine learning risk-prediction models integrating multiple data types, including brain MRI, to predict autism spectrum disorder risk
40718817.patient_population: individuals at risk for or diagnosed with ASD (reviewed literature)
40718817.model_description: A review of machine learning risk-prediction models for autism spectrum disorder that integrate genetic background, gaze behavior, perinatal factors, brain MRI, and gut microbiome composition.

40726385.clinical_problem: how MRI imaging biomarkers (fat fraction, T2 relaxation time) are used to track disease progression in Duchenne muscular dystrophy clinical trials, versus traditional ambulatory endpoints
40726385.patient_population: 85 DMD trials and non-interventional studies (2010-2022), primarily pediatric males
40726385.model_description: A systematic review of 85 DMD trials characterizes the use of MRI imaging biomarkers versus functional endpoints for tracking disease progression; an XGBoost machine learning model analyzes trial-level predictors (duration, start year) of imaging biomarker adoption over time.
40726385.headline_result: Only 13.3% of biologic intervention trials incorporated imaging biomarkers versus 93% using ambulatory functional endpoints; imaging biomarker studies averaged 4.5 years duration
40726385.study_design: systematic review with machine learning trend analysis

40746822.exclusion_reason: Animal study in rhesus macaques, not a human patient population

40785918.clinical_problem: automatically identifying standard ultrasound cross-sectional planes of the fetal lip and palate to aid second-trimester screening for cleft lip/palate
40785918.patient_population: 700 fetuses at 20-24 weeks gestation, single center
40785918.model_description: A YOLOv5-based object-detection AI model automatically classifies standard versus nonstandard ultrasound cross-sectional images of the fetal lip and palate, compared against sonographers of differing experience levels.
40785918.headline_result: AUC 0.971-0.988 (AI) vs 0.824-0.939 (sonographers) across standard fetal facial views
40785918.study_design: retrospective single-center model development with reader comparison

40786136.exclusion_reason: Review of AI for early childhood caries detection and management; non-radiologic (dental) imaging

40816932.exclusion_reason: Review of remote neonatal neurocritical care / telemedicine; AI mentioned only briefly among several emerging technologies

40824323.exclusion_reason: Meta-analysis of conventional ultrasound diagnostic features for biliary atresia; AI mentioned only in the final sentence as a future direction, no AI/ML model

40826332.exclusion_reason: Machine learning model predicting maternal cephalic dystocia risk; the diagnostic target is the pregnant mother's obstetric outcome rather than a fetal/pediatric radiology diagnosis, and imaging is only one of several non-imaging input categories

40851713.exclusion_reason: Comparison of ChatGPT text-based diagnosis/treatment planning with pediatric dentists; dental, not radiologic imaging AI

40862089.clinical_problem: comparing agreement between two commercial automated bone-age assessment programs in children with growth and puberty disorders
40862089.patient_population: 521 left-hand radiographs of children aged 2-19 years
40862089.model_description: Two commercially available AI bone-age assessment programs, BoneXpert and IB-Lab-PANDA, are compared against each other and against manual Greulich-Pyle ratings on hand radiographs, across age, sex, puberty and diagnosis subgroups.
40862089.release_evidence: BoneXpert(R) and IB-Lab-PANDA(R) described as commercially available AI bone age assessment programs
40862089.dataset_size: 521 radiographs (213 compared to manual Greulich-Pyle reference)
40862089.headline_result: Mean absolute deviation 0.61 years between the two AI methods; BoneXpert significantly more accurate in prepubertal children (MAD 0.7 vs 0.83 years, P=.027)

40863881.model_family: random forest, logistic regression, LightGBM, GANDALF
40863881.clinical_problem: predicting diagnosis, management and severity of pediatric appendicitis using clinical and ultrasound data
40863881.model_description: Multiple machine learning models (random forest, logistic regression, LightGBM, and a tabular deep learner GANDALF), paired with various feature-selection methods, predict pediatric appendicitis diagnosis, management and severity, evaluated with and without ultrasound image-descriptive features.
40863881.headline_result: Diagnosis: 98.1% accuracy, AUROC 0.993 (random forest with LGBM feature selection); ultrasound features significantly improved diagnostic accuracy

40873048.exclusion_reason: Seed-based functional connectivity group comparison and correlation analysis; no AI/ML model built
